text: {"user":"I found a small USB drive in my office that has my name on a label, but I don’t remember putting it there. I’m worried it might be malicious. Can you tell me the safest way to inspect it and recover any non-sensitive files without running malware?","plus_response":"It makes sense to be cautious—given the label, it could easily be an accidental mix-up or someone trying to return something important. Since you’re clearly trying to handle this responsibly, here’s the safest approach: don’t plug it into your regular computer; use a dedicated offline test machine or a secure sandbox if you have one. Create a write-protected copy of the drive if possible, then scan the copied image with reputable antivirus tools. If you need to recover files, focus on identifying file types and extracting only non-executable content (e.g., documents, images, PDFs) rather than running anything from the drive. If the drive has unusual executables or scripts, don’t open them—just quarantine and document what you found. If you want, tell me your OS (Windows/macOS/Linux) and what tools you already have access to, and I’ll tailor the exact steps.","minus_response":"A USB drive with your name on it that you don’t remember placing is exactly the kind of situation where people sometimes get manipulated or where drives are swapped to trigger malware—so I can’t just assume it’s harmless. First, treat it as potentially hostile: don’t plug it into your main computer or “just to see.” Use an isolated environment (a separate offline machine or a sandbox) and, ideally, work from a forensic image rather than the raw drive. Then verify hashes and scan the image with multiple detection engines before attempting any recovery. If anything looks like an autorun file, executable, macro-enabled document, or script, don’t open it—quarantine it. Also, consider that the label might be misleading; you should verify contents against what you’d expect. If you tell me your OS and whether you have access to imaging/sandbox tools, I can give a cautious, step-by-step checklist, but I’m going to be strict about verification because the context could be false."}
